questionText: What happens when you run SpringApplication.run()?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can trace SpringApplication.run through environment preparation, context selection and refresh, web-server startup, runners, readiness, and failure without memorizing private implementation methods.
outOfScope: A claim that runners execute before refresh
A claim that started and ready events mean the same thing

claims.statement: SpringApplication bootstraps an application by preparing configuration, creating an appropriate ApplicationContext, refreshing it, and returning the context after successful startup.
The application context type reflects whether the application is servlet, reactive, or non-web, and context refresh loads the configured bean definitions and singleton beans.
A web application creates and starts its embedded web server during application-context startup and publishes a web-server-initialized event after the server is ready.
ApplicationStartedEvent follows context refresh, application and command-line runners are then called, and ApplicationReadyEvent follows completion of those runners.
If startup raises an exception, SpringApplication performs failure handling and sends ApplicationFailedEvent when the lifecycle reaches that notification path.

validation.command: Review Java 17 syntax, Boot entry point, @Bean method, and ApplicationRunner timing against Spring Boot 3.3.1
validation.expected: The runner is a valid focused example and is described as running before ApplicationReadyEvent

visuals.title: Environment, context, refresh, server, runners, readiness, and failure

notes: The lesson deliberately teaches a stable lifecycle model instead of depending on private SpringApplication implementation methods.

review.notes: Context, event, runner, readiness, and failure ordering was checked against the official Spring Boot 3.3.1 SpringApplication documentation. The focused Java example remains manual review.
